An existing file must still be checked against demos when the protocol requires it; never claim it is demo-validated without running those checks. After an incorrect verdict, never repeat the same grid: feedback gives no cell-level diagnosis. Preserve the last-known verified program while testing alternatives; an unverified candidate does not become trusted just because it ran. **An existing file is only a candidate, not proof it is correct for the current task/input.** If its submission is wrong, immediately return to the demo-and-infer workflow; do not keep submitting it or update it with a test-only guess.

Infer from the whole grid before coding: distinguish object outlines from dividers, find the background using both frequency and spatial role, and list candidate objects, bounds, interiors, and any separate marker shapes. For a divider-based pattern, test both full rows and full columns as separators; derive the two panel bounds from the actual divider orientation, then compare corresponding cells only across panels with compatible dimensions. A uniform non-background row or column is only a candidate: a solid line inside a patterned panel can look like a divider and produce plausible-looking but wrong crops. Check candidate positions against the full layout, separator color, and resulting panel extents; prefer the line that explains two coherent, appropriately aligned panels rather than blindly taking the first uniform line. Do not assume a recurring task ID guarantees the same divider axis, colors, or dimensions. Never treat a filled rectangular-looking crop as a valid object without verifying that its full perimeter and interior meet the hypothesized rule.

Infer on all available pairs, not just the most recent: test candidate rules against every demo and reject a hypothesis as soon as any pair contradicts it. Before requesting another pair, name at least two competing rules and predict how their outputs differ on the current test; request only if the new pair can discriminate them enough to justify its cost. If a rule remains uncertain, do not revise an existing program or submit a fabricated variant merely because it ran. Use a demo that separates concrete hypotheses, or spend remaining analysis on the observed pair(s) and submit the best-supported program-produced candidate without claiming validation.

Parse the supplied grid as rows and verify the declared dimensions and uniform row widths before execution; malformed input can cause a misleading transform failure or output. Require exact reproduction of all demos before calling a rule validated or replacing the task file. On mismatch, inspect the first differing coordinates and update the hypothesis; do not keep an implementation that only happens to match the test. Compare output to each demo cell-by-cell, including unchanged background cells, and verify that the motif/template comes from the intended component rather than unrelated border noise. A successful run or plausible-looking grid is not validation. After an incorrect test verdict, first compare the actual submitted output with the demo-derived prediction, then alter only a rule supported by observed evidence; the verdict alone does not identify wrong cells. Check dimensions and cell range, then submit exactly the serialized grid printed by that transform, never a manually transcribed or altered copy. If the evidence leaves competing hypotheses, compare their predicted test grids and choose the best-supported candidate within budget, labeling it unverified.
6. Submit only the exact grid printed by the validated transform. After a correct verdict, save that verified transform to `programs/<task id>.py` and finish. After an incorrect verdict, preserve the prior verified file; update the task file only after the replacement reproduces every received pair and the new test grid has been generated by that version. Never persist or treat a demo-inconsistent guess as a reusable program. If the instance is still active after a wrong submission, continue the task workflow and submit another evidence-based candidate; do not end the turn with commentary or claim completion without the required action object.

Every action must be one supported JSON action on the final line. Attempts and demo requests each have a cost, and unsolved instances incur the full loss; spend demos to resolve output-changing ambiguity, not merely to continue brainstorming. If no hypothesis fits all received pairs, keep investigating and validate rather than presenting an unverified guess as reproduced.

    seen=set(); objs=[]
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if grid[r][c]!=1 or (r,c) in seen: continue
            q=[(r,c)];seen.add((r,c));obj=[]
            while q:
                y,x=q.pop();obj.append((y,x))
                for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    a,b=y+dy,x+dx
                    if 0<=a<h and 0<=b<w and grid[a][b]==1 and (a,b) not in seen:
                        seen.add((a,b));q.append((a,b))
            objs.append(obj)

        r0=min(r for r,c in obj);r1=max(r for r,c in obj)

         if all(all(grid[r][c]==1 for r,c in side) for side in sides):
